transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Lisa Huang (Solace CISO), Tom Rivera (VP Eng), Aisha Khan (DevOps)
Recording link: (internal) https://redwood.app/rec/ff-20260520-solace-001

Summary:
- Solace Medical is evaluating Redwood for clinical triage assistant; primary requirement is strong compliance posture (HIPAA adjacency, SOC2/ISO), strict key management and ability to restrict data flows. They are currently using a mix of OpenAI hosted endpoints and an internal model infra for sensitive workloads.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Carlos, our SE. How are you all?
[00:08] Lisa: Hi, yes thanks. I'm Lisa, CISO at Solace. We got a quick list of questions about security posture, SSO, KMS, that kind of thing.
[00:15] Tom: Tom here, VP Eng. We're trying to map requirements for a vendor that can handle PHI-like PII. Not full HIPAA exchange yet, but close.
[00:25] Maya: Totally. Today we'll cover SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS, and deployment models — hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Carlos will jump into technical details.
[00:35] Carlos: Hey all. Quick note, my audio's a bit low, but I'll start with our compliance stuff. Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report — uh — we can share the redacted report; we also have ISO 27001 in process for a subset of services, and roadmap to expand.
[00:50] Lisa: Can you clarify which controls cover the hosted API? We need evidence of data separation and logging for multi-tenant.
[00:58] Carlos: Yes, for hosted our controls map to typical SOC 2 CC and there is tenant isolation with logical separation. Audit logs capture request metadata, model used, and tokens processed — though we redact sensitive payloads on request. The hosted offering keeps transients by default for X days, and we can configure retention.
[01:15] Aisha: When you say redaction on request, how is that initiated? API flag or contract?
[01:20] Carlos: Good question. Redaction for our hosted product can be controlled via tenant settings and contractual terms. For Dedicated and Private, customers control retention entirely.
[01:28] Lisa: KMS — do you integrate with customer-managed keys? We need to ensure never-exfiltrate keys.
[01:33] Carlos: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations — AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and HSM options for Private. For Dedicated we can integrate into your KMS using a key policy that prevents key export. There's also an HSM-backed option for on-prem where keys never leave the customer boundary.
[01:50] Tom: Is there support for bring-your-own-HSM?
[01:52] Carlos: For Private deployments, yes — BYO-HSM supported. For Dedicated in shared hardware setups, HSM tokens can be managed per-tenant via our key management broker.
[02:05] [02:05] Maya: On SSO — do you do SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
[02:10] Carlos: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Role sync for RBAC maps to SCIM groups. There's some small setup on our side to map your IdP claims to Redwood roles.
[02:20] Lisa: We need SAML with IdP initiated login and MFA enforcement. Is that supported?
[02:25] Carlos: Yes, IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows are supported. For enforcement of MFA, that's handled at the IdP level; we accept the assertion.
[02:33] Aisha: For audit logs, what's the retention and can they be exported to our SIEM?
[02:38] Carlos: Logs are stored by default for 90 days on hosted, can be extended with add-on. You can stream logs to your SIEM via an event export or forward logs to a customer S3/GCP bucket for dedicated/private. For Private, logs remain under your control.
[02:51] Tom: And what about immutable logs or WORM requirements?
[02:54] Carlos: We support write-once mode when exporting to customer storage, so you can enforce immutability on your end. For hosted, we have append-only internal logs for compliance but the immutable/WORM is generally customer-managed through export.
[03:08] Lisa: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain workloads and US-only for others. Can you pin region for both serving and control plane?
[03:17] Carlos: For Dedicated we can pin serving in a particular region and restrict egress. For Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) the control plane can be customer-managed and hosted in-region; for hosted API we offer region-specific endpoints but the control plane remains Redwood-hosted — we do offer contractual guarantees about residency for certain enterprise plans.
[03:36] Maya: The distinction is important — hosted is easiest but control plane resides in our managed service; Dedicated gives you isolated capacity and stronger guarantees; Private gives full customer control including KMS and control plane.
[03:49] Tom: For Dedicated, is network peering supported?
[03:52] Carlos: Yes, we support VPC peering and PrivateLink equivalents, and we have a checklist for firewall rules, IP allowlists, and egress policies. We'll share the peering guide.
[04:01] Lisa: Encryption at rest and in transit — are both mandatory? What ciphers?
[04:07] Carlos: All traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest we default to AES-256. When you use customer-managed KMS keys, keys are used for envelope encryption.
[04:18] Aisha: Token handling — does Redwood store prompts/responses? For PHI we can't keep raw text.
[04:24] Carlos: By default hosted may store for short-term caching and quality/regression monitoring; however we offer an option to disable storage and enable just-in-time processing or customer-managed retention. For Dedicated/Private you can disable all retention. We also offer token-level redaction for PII if you supply regex or a set of rules.
[04:42] Lisa: How is RBAC structured? We need least-privilege roles and auditable admin actions.
[04:47] Carlos: RBAC is role-based with prebuilt roles (Admin, Dev, Viewer) and custom roles. All admin actions are logged with actor, timestamp, and IP. We also support scoped API keys with specific route permissions to limit what services a token can call.
[05:01] Tom: Is there session recording or session replay? We won't need that but need to ensure it's disabled by default.
[05:06] Carlos: No session replay by default. Audit logs capture metadata, not full session transcripts unless requested and contracted.
[05:14] [05:14] Maya: I wanted to call out one common ask — model fallbacks and graceful degradation. If a model variant is used for cost or latency reasons, we surface that in logs for traceability.
[05:25] Lisa: Good, we need traceability. On the contractual side, do you have breach notification timelines and incident response SLAs?
[05:32] Maya: Our contract standard includes 72-hour notification for incidents and we offer SOC-based incident handling; for enterprise we can negotiate tighter terms.
[05:40] Aisha: For on-prem/private, what are the operational footprints? Containers? Full appliance?
[05:45] Carlos: Private can be delivered as a customer-managed control plane running in your VPC (helm charts / operators), or as an on-prem appliance for air-gapped environments. It needs GPUs for inference; we have recommended instance types and a sizing guide. We'll attach the Sizing + Ops doc.
[05:59] Tom: Benchmarks — can we run a short perf test? We want 95th percentile latency below 300ms for small prompts.
[06:06] Carlos: Yes, we can coordinate a perf run. For Dedicated we can provision a small cluster for benchmarking; for Private we'd ship a test harness. We'll need sample workload and sequence length distribution.
[06:18] Lisa: Any certifications for healthcare specifically? You mentioned SOC2 and ISO. HIPAA is not certified but you have controls that map — is Redwood willing to sign a BAA?
[06:26] Maya: We have customers in healthcare and we are willing to negotiate a BAA for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we evaluate on a case-by-case basis — we'll follow up with legal.
[06:36] Aisha: Who handles vulnerability scanning and patching on Dedicated?
[06:40] Carlos: For Dedicated we manage the runtime and patching; there's a shared responsibility model for the OS-level patching of customer-provided nodes if you're hosting. For Private (customer-managed control plane) patching is customer or co-managed depending on the support tier.
[06:54] Tom: Is there support for hardware-attested boot and secure enclave?
[06:58] Carlos: We have roadmap items for confidential compute and attestation (TPM/SEV). For Private you can integrate with enclave-backed instances. I'll flag this as a requirement.
[07:08] Lisa: Ok, let's talk next steps and what you need from us.
[07:12] Maya: Great — high level of asks: we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts; Carlos will prepare a VPC/private checklist and KMS integration notes; we need your network diagram and compliance contact. We'll also schedule a SE-led deep dive to run perf benchmarks.
[07:26] Tom: Sounds good. We'll pull together the network diagram and compliance requirements and aim to get that by next Friday.
[07:33] Lisa: Also please send the SAML docs, SCIM mapping guidance.
[07:36] Carlos: Will do. I'll include examples.
[07:40] Maya: Any final questions?
[07:42] Lisa: One last — do you log model prompts verbatim for debug by default? We need an option to never persist.
[07:47] Carlos: By default there is short-term retention for logged prompts for quality but we support a never-persist option and redaction rules; for Dedicated/Private you control persistence.
[07:57] Maya: Great — recap of next steps on screen.
[08:00] [End-of-call recap]
- Maya: Send SOC2, ISO artifacts (Maya)
- Carlos: VPC/Private deployment checklist, KMS notes, SAML/SCIM examples
- Solace: Share network diagram and compliance contact
- Schedule: SE deep dive + perf run (tentative week of 2026-05-25)
